Terry Sawchuk was a Ukrainian-Canadian goaltender and one of the greatest netminders in hockey history. His one hundred three shutouts remain an NHL record, and his four hundred forty-seven wins defined excellence in goal during an era of monster workloads and minimal equipment protection.

He recorded one hundred three career shutouts in nine hundred seventy-one games, the most in NHL history and unlikely to be approached in the modern era with today's scoring rates. Sawchuk won four Stanley Cups with the Detroit Red Wings in nineteen fifty-two, nineteen fifty-four, nineteen fifty-five, and nineteen fifty-seven, and one with the Toronto Maple Leafs in nineteen sixty-seven. At his peak, he played roughly forty or more games per season, facing brutal workloads without modern backup systems, and recorded multiple seasons with sub-two-point-zero zero goals-against averages.

He won the Vezina Trophy for best goaltender four times and the Hart Trophy for MVP once, the only goaltender to win MVP in the post-nineteen sixty era. Sawchuk was known for his aggressive, acrobatic style and willingness to leave the crease to handle the puck. He suffered multiple career-threatening injuries including a serious eye injury. He played with minimal mask protection for much of his career, enduring facial cuts, broken noses, and other trauma from ungloved shots. Late in his career at age thirty-six, he won the Stanley Cup with the Toronto Maple Leafs in nineteen sixty-seven, proving his durability across eras.
